macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks finish mixed as earnings offset AI concerns
items.summary: The Dow rose 529.85 points, or 1.02%, to 52,495.88, while the S&P 500 gained 0.28% to 7,712.57 and the Nasdaq slipped 0.02% to 26,424.82. Strong corporate results supported stocks, but investors remained concerned about debt-fueled AI investment and credit risks.

items.title: Oil prices retreat, easing inflation and bond-market pressure
items.summary: Brent crude fell 0.7% to $108.79 a barrel after approaching its highest level since the war with Iran began. The 10-year Treasury yield declined to roughly 5.12%, while the 30-year yield also fell, although the two-year yield rose slightly.

items.title: Fed rate-hike expectations decline
items.summary: Markets priced a 17.2% probability of at least a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate increase at next week’s meeting, down from 22.1% a week earlier and 57.6% a month earlier.

items.title: Equifax, Hasbro and 3M rally on strong earnings
items.summary: Equifax jumped 11.3% after exceeding summer-quarter profit expectations, Hasbro gained 11.2% after reporting record quarterly Magic: The Gathering revenue, and 3M rose 5.8% after beating estimates and raising its full-year profit forecast.

items.title: GM falls despite earnings beat and announces major buyback
items.summary: General Motors shares dropped 6.8% even after the automaker reported stronger-than-expected profit. GM also announced a program to return up to $20 billion to investors through share repurchases.

items.title: Netflix slides after lowering outlook
items.summary: Netflix shares fell more than 5% despite an earnings beat after the company reduced its fiscal 2026 outlook for overall revenue and advertising sales.

items.title: SpaceX reports sharp revenue growth and considers Tesla merger
items.summary: SpaceX shares rose after the company reported third-quarter revenue of $14.575 billion, up 161% year over year, and net income of $4.4 billion. The company said a special committee would examine potential merger matters involving Tesla.

items.title: Weak U.S. housing data weighs on growth outlook
items.summary: Contract signings for home purchases fell in September to a record low as the average 30-year mortgage rate moved above 7%. The housing weakness contributed to lower Treasury yields and reinforced concerns about the effects of elevated borrowing costs.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: France backs 31.4% tax on crypto-to-stablecoin swaps
items.summary: France’s National Assembly narrowly approved an amendment that would tax crypto-to-stablecoin conversions at 31.4% from January 2027, subject to the broader finance bill becoming law.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $83,000 as crypto market recovers
items.summary: Bitcoin briefly climbed above $83,000 and was recently reported near $82,600, up about 0.8% over 24 hours. Ether also advanced roughly 1.6% to around $2,438.

items.title: U.S. Senate fails to advance CLARITY Act
items.summary: The Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act failed to clear a Senate procedural vote by 49–50, leaving a major U.S. cryptocurrency-market regulatory framework stalled.

items.title: Switzerland approves first retail spot Bitcoin ETF
items.summary: Swiss regulator FINMA reportedly approved the country’s first retail spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund, creating a regulated Bitcoin investment vehicle for ordinary investors.

items.title: Qubic halts mainnet after wallet drain
items.summary: Qubic suspended its mainnet following a wallet-drain incident affecting 1,404 accounts, while other blockchain projects reported new product and trading developments.

items.title: Pump.fun expands into perpetual futures
items.summary: Pump.fun introduced perpetual-futures trading powered by Hyperliquid, marking a significant expansion from token launches into decentralized derivatives markets.

items.title: Mt. Gox repayment deadline delayed again
items.summary: Mt. Gox trustee Nobuaki Kobayashi received court approval to postpone creditor repayments by another year, moving the deadline to October 31, 2027.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: NVIDIA releases Cosmos3-H-Dreams surgical world model
items.summary: NVIDIA reportedly released Cosmos3-H-Dreams, an action-conditioned generative world model designed for real-time robotic surgery and fine-tuned on clinical recordings from the Versius surgical system.

items.title: llm-d 1.0 targets production-scale AI inference
items.summary: The llm-d 1.0 release consolidates an open framework for distributed large-language-model inference, focusing on serving efficiency, scalability, and day-two production operations.

items.title: MiniMax and DeepSeek introduce cheaper, faster agent models
items.summary: MiniMax launched M3.1 Flash, claiming substantially higher inference speed and lower agent-task costs, while DeepSeek updated its V4.1-Flash-1017 model to improve speed, coding, reasoning, and agent workloads.

items.title: China-U.S. tensions deepen over DeepSeek restrictions
items.summary: China criticized a U.S. ban on DeepSeek products for federal civilian agencies, while broader technology tensions continue around AI, chips, and export controls.

items.title: AI agents gain momentum as downloads surge
items.summary: Downloads of consumer AI agents, including Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s dots, are reportedly increasing rapidly, highlighting a shift toward task-oriented AI applications.

items.title: NVIDIA CEO urges German manufacturers to adopt AI
items.summary: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang called on German manufacturers to combine industrial expertise with AI and digital technologies to modernize production and economic activity.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: EA Sports revives Fight Night boxing franchise
items.summary: EA Sports announced the return of the Fight Night series, which has been dormant since Fight Night Champion in 2011. The publisher provided no release date, platforms, gameplay details, or clarification on whether the project is a new game or remaster.[3][10]

items.title: Xbox and IGN showcase highlights upcoming indie games
items.summary: The ID@Xbox and IGN showcase revealed A Game About Digging a Hole Together and Magenta Down, while also announcing additional indie titles coming to Xbox. Arctic Eggs became available on Xbox on the same day.[8]

items.title: Survey examines GTA VI’s potential cultural and economic impact
items.summary: A GameSquare survey of 1,000 U.S. employees who identify as gamers found that 30% may take time off for Grand Theft Auto VI, while 84% intend to buy it. Rockstar lists November 19 as the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S release date.[1][2]
